stages.title: CHRONOLOGY FROM AURANGZEB TO THE 1740S
sequence: 1707 Aurangzeb dies → Bahadur Shah I 1707-12 → Jahandar Shah 1712-13
1713 Farrukhsiyar rises with Sayyid support → 1719 deposition and enthronements
1720 Sayyids fall → 1724 Nizam's Hyderabad autonomy → 1739 Karnal and Delhi
1740s → regional bargaining and frontier pressure; later Durrani/Panipat stay bounded.

stages.title: SUCCESSION INSTABILITY: THRONE BECOMES A PRIZE

pills.text: PRINCES MOBILISE HOUSEHOLDS AND NOBLE CLIENTS
VICTORY REALLOCATES MANSAB, JAGIR AND OFFICE
EMPEROR CANNOT CREDIBLY ARBITRATE ELITE COMPETITION

sequence: NO FIXED PRIMOGENITURE → princes mobilise households and noble clients
SUCCESSION WAR → victory reallocates mansab, jagir and office
REPEATED CONTEST → emperor cannot credibly arbitrate elite competition
RESULT → political transmission fails; it is a mechanism, not a lone cause.

stages.title: FISCAL-MILITARY FEEDBACK LOOP

pills.text: UNPAID CONTINGENTS AND WEAKER IMPERIAL SERVICE

sequence: MORE CLAIMANTS + WEAK PAIBAQI → scramble for productive jagirs
SHORT TENURE / EXTRACTION → resistance, evasion, flight or negotiation
LOWER HASIL → unpaid contingents and weaker imperial service
WEAKER CONTROL → regional retention of revenue → still lower central capacity.

stages.title: AURANGZEB'S LEGACY: A WEIGHTED BACKGROUND

pills.text: GARRISONS, TRANSPORT, REMOUNTS AND UNRESOLVED MARATHA CHALLENGE
TERRITORY AND CLAIMS GROW FASTER THAN RELIABLE REALISATION
LEGACY MATTERED, BUT AURANGZEB ALONE CANNOT EXPLAIN POST-1707 FACTIONS

sequence: DECCAN WAR → garrisons, transport, remounts and unresolved Maratha challenge
ANNEXATIONS → territory and claims grow faster than reliable realisation
NORTH ABSENCE → strains of supervision and arbitration
QUALIFY → legacy mattered, but Aurangzeb alone cannot explain post-1707 factions or regions.

stages.title: AGRARIAN AND REGIONAL ASSERTION

pills.text: ZAMINDARS, PEASANTS AND INTERMEDIARIES BARGAIN OR RESIST
DISTINCT POLITICAL ROUTES, NOT ONE REBELLION
DELHI'S WEAKENING AND REGIONAL STATE-MAKING REINFORCE EACH OTHER.

sequence: REVENUE PRESSURE → zamindars, peasants and intermediaries bargain or resist
GOVERNORS + BANKERS + ARMED FOLLOWINGS → provincial resource control
MARATHA / SIKH / JAT mobilisation → distinct political routes, not one rebellion
RESULT → Delhi's weakening and regional state-making reinforce each other.

stages.title: NADIR SHAH: SHOCK EXPOSES A PRIOR CRISIS

pills.text: FRAGMENTED COMMAND LOSES TO UNIFIED COMMAND
SACK, TREASURY LOSS AND PRESTIGE SHOCK; MUHAMMAD SHAH REMAINS
ACCELERANT AND REVEALER, NOT THE ORIGINAL CAUSE OF DECLINE.

sequence: FRONTIER WEAKNESS + Persian military capacity → invasion opportunity
KARNAL, 24 FEBRUARY 1739 → fragmented command loses to unified command
DELHI → sack, treasury loss and prestige shock; Muhammad Shah remains emperor
VERDICT → accelerant and revealer, not the original cause of decline.
CLOSE DISTINCTION: Decline of enforceable central command did not mean instant state collapse
